interface.title: AxoDen (v1.1.0), Streamlit app
interface.field: Neuroscience / neuroanatomy: fluorescence histology of axonal projections
interface.stage_of_work: Image quantification and figure generation after microscopy and region-of-interest masking
interface.what_it_is_for: Measures the percent of a masked brain region covered by axonal fluorescence signal, using Otsu thresholding on uploaded .tif images, and returns summary tables, bar plots, profiles along the medio-lateral and dorso-ventral axes, and per-image control plots that can be downloaded as PDF.

data.note: Uploaded the four bundled test images 745_TH-CL.tif, 745_TH-CM.tif, 745_TH-MD.tif and 746_TH-CL.tif (thalamus, already masked). The file names have no group part, so the app filled group as 'group1'. Results at the default 0.75521 µm pixel size: 745 TH-CL 24.05%, 746 TH-CL 36.97%, TH-CM 0.51%, TH-MD 0.28% signal. The Otsu thresholds were 21.95, 31.07, 20 and 20.

tree.general: Measure how densely axons innervate defined regions and compare regions and subjects
tree.specific: Quantify percent-area axonal signal in thalamic sub-regions (TH-CL, TH-CM, TH-MD) for animals 745 and 746 with AxoDen

features.name: Batch image upload with automatic re-analysis
features.general: Drop a batch of images into one uploader. Analysis runs at once with a progress bar. Removing or adding a file re-runs it and updates every result.
features.specific: 'Upload image here' file uploader (.tif/.tiff, up to 100 files and 200 MB) with a paginated file list and × buttons. Each change re-runs the Otsu analysis with 'Processing image n/N' (the replay saw the bar during a re-run, not the first upload).
steps: Press Browse files and select several .tif files
Watch the 'Processing image n/N' progress bar while the analysis runs
Page through the uploaded-file list
Press × on a file to drop it; the summary N and the table rows update
Browse again to add files to the existing set
serves_tasks: Load the image set, which starts the analysis automatically
Change which images are included and re-run

features.name: Calibration and masking settings that recompute results
features.general: Set the physical scale and say whether images are pre-cropped. All area measurements and thresholds recompute live.
features.specific: Pixel Size (µm) number input (with a ± stepper of 0.01) and a note listing 4x/20x values, plus the 'Images are masked' checkbox. Changing pixel size rescales the area columns (about 25× from 20x to 4x) but leaves % innervation unchanged. Unticking the mask makes the analysis count the whole image, so the thresholds change.
steps: Type a pixel size
Watch the summary areas rescale
Untick 'Images are masked' to analyse the whole image
Compare pixels_total and threshold in the table
Tick it again to restore
serves_tasks: Set the physical pixel size that matches the acquisition optics
Say whether images are already cropped to the region of interest

features.name: Per-image segmentation control plots in nested tabs
features.general: Look through each item's raw image, binary segmentation, mask and signal fraction, grouped by category, to judge whether the threshold is trustworthy. Then export them all.
features.specific: Control Plots by Brain Area: one tab per brain region and one numbered sub-tab per animal. Each shows the grayscale image, the binarized image (both with axis intensity margins), the mask, and a pie chart of the area with and without projections. The heading line gives animal, area in mm², group and threshold. 'Download plots as pdf' exports all of them.
steps: Pick a brain-region tab
Pick an animal sub-tab when the region has more than one image
Compare the binarized image against the grayscale and the mask
Read area and threshold in the heading line
Press Download plots as pdf
serves_tasks: Compare each raw image against its threshold mask and binarized signal
Save the summary and quality-control figures as files
features.note: Caveat: after switching to the 4x pixel size and unticking 'Images are masked', the summary figure and table updated but the control plots still showed Area 0.10 mm² and the masked mask (screens/027.webp, screens/028.webp). Re-check the control plots after changing settings. The reviewer, reading the code, notes that process_image_single_cached is keyed on pixel_size and is_masked and suggests the pdf_viewer's fixed key as the likely cause; this was not tested. The tutorial calls the export button 'Download figure as pdf'; the app labels it 'Download plots as pdf'.

features.name: Group summary figure with tidy results table
features.general: Show the group means ± SEM of the main measure and two sanity-check measures per category, with a tidy per-item table you can search, sort and view full screen, and export the figure.
features.specific: Summary Data: four panels (Percentage of innervation, Area of the brain region, Threshold for binarization, Animals per Brain Region) above an interactive table (animal, brain_area, group, pixel counts, threshold, areas, percent_signal) with download/search/fullscreen tools that appear on hover, plus 'Download figure as pdf'.
steps: Press fullscreen on the figure to read the bars
Press fullscreen on the table to see all columns
Click a column header to sort
Press search and type an animal ID
Press Download figure as pdf
serves_tasks: Compare percent innervation, region area and threshold across regions
Save the summary and quality-control figures as files

features.name: Spatial intensity profiles along two axes
features.general: Plot how signal is spread along two orthogonal anatomical axes for each category, with individual traces and a mean ± SEM band, plus the raw arrays.
features.specific: Summary Data Axis: medio-lateral and dorso-ventral signal-intensity profiles per brain region (grey lines are animals, blue line and band are mean ± SEM), with a table holding the signal_bin_x_ax and signal_bin_y_ax arrays and a PDF download.
steps: Scroll to Summary Data Axis
Press fullscreen to read the profiles for each region
Open the axis table in fullscreen to see the per-animal arrays
Press Download figure as pdf
serves_tasks: Inspect how signal is spread along two anatomical axes (medio-lateral and dorso-ventral)

screens_never_reached: Error or warning state for a badly named or multi-channel image: no such test file was available
Upload-limit warning (over 100 images or 200 MB) that suggests batching or the standalone app: not triggered with four test files
Control plots recomputed for the 4x pixel size or the unmasked mode: the plots stayed at 0.10 mm² and the masked appearance after those settings changed (screens/027.webp, screens/028.webp)
not_done: Preparing images (atlas overlay, ImageJ mask and crop, contrast, subjectID_brainregion_group naming): only read about on the tutorial page; the bundled test images were already masked.

Saving either table as CSV for your own statistics: pressing 'Download as CSV' (screens/016.webp) produced no file in this headless browser. The Streamlit grid's own CSV export may not work in this browser.
Checking the PDF contents: the downloaded PDFs could only be confirmed by file name and size (control_plots.pdf is 309 KB). The reader returns binary files as size only.

Pixel-size stepper: after the + press (screens/029.webp shows 0.7652100000000001) the − stepper was pressed to return to 0.75521, but no kept screen shows the restored value, so the stepper actions were dropped from t4. Areas shown after this point may be at 0.76521 unless the − press took effect; % signal is unaffected.

Possible stale display: after switching to the 4x pixel size and unticking 'Images are masked', the summary figure and table updated, but the control plots did not. They still showed Area 0.10 mm² and the masked mask (screens/027.webp, screens/028.webp), which looks like caching. Not investigated further.
Comparing experimental groups: all test files lack a group part in their names, so every image was assigned 'group1' and no comparison between groups was possible.

open_fixes: Table CSV export task: not added because 'Download as CSV' produced no file here; a run in a browser where the download works is needed to show and cite the result.
Group comparison task: not added because every test file lacked a group segment; a run with files named subjectID_brainregion_group.tif across two or more groups is needed.
Actual image-preparation tasks (atlas overlay, ImageJ masking, cropping, contrast): not added because the run only read the tutorial; a run that prepares raw images is needed to show them.
Pixel-size stepper: a new run should screenshot the value after the − press to confirm it returns to 0.75521.
Upload-limit handling (100 files / 200 MB warning): needs a run with an oversized batch to reach and cite the warning.
Control-plot staleness: needs a run that changes pixel size or masking and then reloads the control plots, to confirm the stale display and whether the pdf_viewer's key is the cause.
